diagnostic_evidence.quote: $\tau^{S}(x) := e_{1}(x)\wedge \dots e_{m}(x)$, a wedge product of orthonomal basis vectors of the tangent space at $x$
$\wedge$ is antisymmetric, so that for $x,y \in V$, $\wedge (x,y) = -\wedge (y,x)$
the unique current associated with it is defined as $[S]\in  \Omega_{0}^{m}(\R^{d})^{*}$

issues.failure_explanation: For $m\geq 1$, replacing the orthonormal basis $(e_1,\dots,e_m)$ of the tangent space by an orientation-reversing one multiplies $\tau^S(x)=e_1\wedge\dots\wedge e_m$ by $-1$, since the wedge product is alternating (antisymmetry is stated in the paper's own appendix). The claimed invariance holds only for orientation-preserving changes, so the integrand in the definition of $[S]$, and hence $[S]$ itself, is defined only up to sign unless an orientation of the rectifiable set is fixed. The 'unique current' and the well-definedness claim are therefore false as stated, and the same gap is inherited by the abstract definition $N(S)=[\mathcal{N}_S]$.

failure_location.quote: This is well defined, as the tangent space exists $\mathcal{H}^{m}$ a.e. for a $m$-Hausdorff rectifiable set, and the choice of basis vectors does not matter due to invariance of wedge product under change of orthonomal basis.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add an orientation (an orienting $m$-vector field) to the definition of $[S]$ and replace the invariance claim by invariance under orientation-preserving changes of orthonormal basis; all subsequent concrete formulas are unaffected.
issues.overall_effect: The abstractly defined currents $[S]$ and normal cycles $N(S)$ are only defined up to sign, and the dual-space distances built on them depend on the orientation choice. The concrete triangulated-surface computations later fix orientations implicitly, so no labelled downstream result fails solely from this gap.
issues.title: Current [S] is ill-defined: wedge product is not invariant under orientation-reversing change of orthonormal basis
issues.why_classification: A standard local hypothesis addition fixes the ill-definedness; the method, conclusions, and advertised scope all survive unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: $A_{i} = \sum_{k}{f_{k}^{i}/\lvert f_{k}^{i}\rvert}$ is the sum of normalized edges oriented outwards from vertex $x_{i}$
This expression has the generic form $\mu = \sum_{i=1}^{n}{\delta_{x_{i}}\alpha_{i}} \in V^{*},\quad x_{i} \in \R^{d}, \quad \alpha \in \R^{k}$

issues.failure_explanation: Section 3.1 asserts $N(C)=\sum_i\delta_{x_i}A_i$ and $N(S)=\sum_j\delta_{y_j}B_j$ with the same $A_i,B_j$ (sums of normalized outward edge vectors) as in Theorem thm:added-2. The reproducing-kernel computation of the $W^*$ inner product of these two functionals gives $\sum_{i,j}k_p(x_i,y_j)\langle A_i,B_j\rangle$ with no extra factor, whereas thm:added-2 states the inner product is $\frac{\pi^2}{4}\sum_{i,j}k_p(x_i,y_j)\langle A_i,B_j\rangle$. The two displayed claims differ by a factor $\pi^2/4\approx 2.47$ and cannot both hold: the representation would need a $\frac{\pi}{2}$ factor (up to sign) to match the theorem. Since this bare representation is the object fed to the compression pipeline (the generic form $\mu=\sum\delta_{x_i}\alpha_i$), the compressed curve normal-cycles reproduce a metric scaled by $4/\pi^2$ relative to the paper's own Theorem (or the Theorem's constant is wrong).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert the missing constant in the curve Dirac representation (e.g. $N(C)=\frac{\pi}{2}\sum_i\delta_{x_i}A_i$, consistent with thm:added-2), or correspondingly correct the constant in thm:added-2; a one-line constant fix that preserves the pipeline and all guarantees.
issues.overall_effect: All curve normal-cycle inner products, distances, gradients, and LDDMM discrepancy terms computed from the (compressed) Dirac representation are mis-scaled by a constant factor relative to the normal-cycle metric of thm:added-2; the claim of compressing the normal cycle of a discrete curve fails as stated for curves.
issues.title: Curve Dirac representation $N(C)=\sum\delta_{x_i}A_i$ is inconsistent with Theorem thm:added-2 (missing constant)
issues.why_classification: The repair is a routine constant insertion with a forced target (agreement with the paper's own theorem); no inference, construction, rate, or guarantee needs repair.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: where $\beta_{T}$ is defined as the unitary vector orthogonal to the edge $e$, lying in the same plane as $T$, and oriented inwards to $T$

issues.failure_explanation: $C$ is half of a great circle of the unit sphere ($S^{+,\perp}_{a,b}= (\mathbb{S}^{d-1}\cap a^\perp)\cap\{u: u\cdot b\geq 0\}$), so $\int_C u\,d\mathcal{H}^1(u)=2\beta$ where $\beta$ is the unit bisector: parametrizing a semicircle $u(\theta)=(\cos\theta,\sin\theta)$, $\theta\in[0,\pi]$, gives $\int u\,d\theta=(0,2)$, of magnitude $2$, not $\pi/2\approx 1.57$. The claimed value $\frac{\pi}{2}\beta_T$ is therefore false. The constant $\frac{\pi}{2}$ in the derived cylindrical Dirac form $N(\mathcal{T})^{cyl}=-\frac{\pi}{2}\sum_j\delta_{c_j}\gamma_j$, and in the edge terms of NC_delta and realembedding, is consequently unsupported: with the correct value $2$, the edge contribution to the $W^*$ metric carries factor $4$ rather than $(\pi/2)^2=\pi^2/4$, so the edge term cannot agree with thm:added-1's $\frac{\pi^2}{4}$ as claimed.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the half-circle integral to $2\beta_T$ and recompute the cylindrical constant in $N(\mathcal{T})^{cyl}$, NC_delta and realembedding (edge coefficient becomes $2$); the resulting edge metric constant $4$ must then be reconciled with the $\pi^2/4$ stated in thm:added-1, which cannot be decided from the source alone.
issues.overall_effect: The absolute scale of the cylindrical (edge) component of the central Dirac decomposition NC_delta and of the real-valued embedding realembedding is unreliable; the claimed consistency of the decomposition with thm:added-1's first sum is unestablished; surface normal-cycle distances and gradients computed from the compression pipeline inherit a wrong constant on all edge contributions.
issues.title: False half-circle unit-normal integral ($\frac{\pi}{2}\beta_T$ instead of $2\beta_T$) makes the cylindrical constant in NC_delta unsupported
issues.why_classification: The fix is a contained recomputation of a constant and the decomposition method and compression guarantees survive, but it breaks the claimed agreement with the cited metric formula and the correct absolute constant cannot be settled from the source; more than a routine typo, well short of architectural loss.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: one may check the resulting scalar product of $N(\mathcal{T}),N(\mathcal{T}') \in W^{*}$ of \cref{NC_delta} agrees with \cref{NC_disc_met}

issues.failure_explanation: The spherical-component derivation applies the (correct) hemisphere integral $\int_{S^+_\alpha}u\,d\mathcal{H}^2=\pi\alpha$ to the half-spheres of boundarysph, giving $N(\mathcal{T})^{sph}=-\pi\sum\delta_{x_k}\alpha_k$ and hence a boundary term $\pi^2\sum k_p(x_i,y_j)\langle A_i,B_j\rangle$ in the inner product induced by NC_delta. But thm:added-1 states the boundary term with coefficient $\frac{\pi^2}{4}$ (corresponding to a representation constant $\frac{\pi}{2}$), and realembedding separately states the boundary coefficient as $\frac{\pi}{2}$ — half of NC_delta's $\pi$. These statements are mutually incompatible: the claimed check that the scalar product of NC_delta 'agrees with NC_disc_met' fails on the boundary term by a factor of 4 even accepting all of the paper's own component formulas, and at least one of {spherical derivation, NC_delta, realembedding, thm:added-1} is wrong.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Determine the correct boundary constant and state it consistently in $N(\mathcal{T})^{sph}$, NC_delta and realembedding — either $\pi$ everywhere (making thm:added-1's boundary coefficient $\pi^2$) or $\frac{\pi}{2}$ everywhere (which requires locating the factor-2 discrepancy in the spherical derivation or in boundarysph); the source alone does not determine which repair is correct.
issues.overall_effect: The boundary (spherical) part of the surface normal-cycle representation is mis-scaled by an undetermined factor of 2 in the representation (4 in the metric); the verification claim linking NC_delta to thm:added-1 is false on the boundary term; realembedding's boundary weights contradict NC_delta's, so compressed surface normal-cycle boundary terms are mis-scaled whichever of the two formulas is used.
issues.title: Boundary/spherical coefficient mutually inconsistent across NC_delta ($\pi$), realembedding ($\pi/2$) and thm:added-1 ($\pi^2/4$)
issues.why_classification: A contained constant reconciliation that preserves the decomposition and the compression pipeline, but the correct value cannot be decided from the source and the claimed agreement with the cited theorem must be re-established; more than a routine typo, but no architectural loss or major weakening.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: one may check the resulting scalar product of $N(\mathcal{T}),N(\mathcal{T}') \in W^{*}$ of \cref{NC_delta} agrees with \cref{NC_disc_met}

issues.failure_explanation: The cylindrical section defines $\gamma_j$ without a leading minus and derives $N(\mathcal{T})^{cyl}=-\frac{\pi}{2}\sum_j\delta_{c_j}\gamma_j$. In NC_delta the symbol is redefined with the opposite sign ($\gamma_i:=-\sum_T(\dots)$) while the coefficient is simultaneously changed from $-\frac{\pi}{2}$ to $\pi$; hence NC_delta's cylindrical part equals $-\pi\sum_j\delta_{c_j}\gamma_j^{cyl}$, which is exactly twice the derived value. The master formula therefore does not follow from the paper's own derivation: its edge contribution to the inner product is $\pi^2\sum k_p\langle f_i,g_j\rangle\langle\sum n_{T,f_i},\sum n_{T,g_j}\rangle$ rather than thm:added-1's $\frac{\pi^2}{4}$ times the same quantity, so the claimed agreement also fails on the edge term by a factor of 4.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change the edge coefficient in NC_delta (and in realembedding) from $\pi$ to $\frac{\pi}{2}$ so that, with the redefined sign-flipped $\gamma$, it matches the cylindrical section's derived result and restores agreement with thm:added-1's first sum.
issues.overall_effect: As written, the central Dirac decomposition NC_delta (and the edge term of realembedding, which repeats the coefficient $\pi$) mis-states the derived cylindrical component by a factor of 2, so the object fed to the compression algorithm is not the derived normal cycle and all surface normal-cycle quantities computed from the pipeline are scaled wrongly on edge contributions; the claimed consistency with thm:added-1 is false.
issues.title: NC_delta's edge coefficient contradicts the paper's own cylindrical derivation by a factor of 2
issues.why_classification: A single local constant correction with a forced target (the paper's own derivation); all substantive claims, guarantees, and scope are preserved once aligned.
